answer: Memory-hard graph walks resist Sybil attacks in AI-agent economies by binding each identity to a committed multi-gigabyte graph. At random epochs, verifiers trigger a synchronized gale of challenges requiring sequential reads from a chosen vertex and Merkle proofs before a tight cutoff. Time-slicing one memory bus misses the deadline, forcing attackers to fund dedicated DRAM capacity per account rather than fanning an ember of cheap clones, though network jitter can cause false rejections.
